entries.title: Active context, close, minimize, resize and descendants
entries.where: Master controller → Active context. Click the intended frame first.
entries.behavior: Actions target the clicked/focused frame. Esc steps out one field/popup level before minimizing; active MS has priority. W resizes/restores, M minimizes/restores, X closes, D toggles descendants, subject to saved bindings. Resized windows retain projected bounds and themed borders across focus and minimize/reopen. W restores retained original geometry. Projection styling is independent of React/Rnd wrapper updates. Left-clicking empty space dismisses all open contextual dials and requested dial editors, consuming that press so it does not also draw or begin a world gesture. Dial ×/close buttons are removed; the middle circle remains an unlabelled origin marker at full opacity. Category Back and Escape still step outward. Controls and rendered target roles retain their own click handling. Empty-space dismissal preserves chosen presets and accepted settings. Registered geometry surfaces now supply target adapters to the same commands and shortcuts; frame-only controls remain frame-only. MC discovers contextual controls from the command catalog rather than a parallel geometry toolbar. Delete selection and Compact are projected there. Popup/value-field Escape still precedes geometry scope and its parent frame.

steps.do: Open a frame, click a value field, edit it, then press Esc.
steps.expect: The value edit cancels and focus returns to its parent.

steps.do: Press Esc again at frame level; reopen it. Try M, W, then W again.
steps.expect: The frame minimizes/restores; resize can restore its earlier size.

steps.do: Expand several nested sections, then invoke Expand / collapse active descendants.
steps.expect: Descendant sections collapse together. Closing preserves reopenable frames.

steps.do: Resize with Shift+W, hover Full viewport and release Shift. Click the window body, minimize/re-expand it several times, then press W.
steps.expect: No extra white wrapper border or unexpected position jump. Expanded cycles return to the selected viewport; W restores original size and position.

entries.limits: Website viewport sizing, not OS/browser fullscreen. Pinned frames reject resizing. Projected frames use W restore before dragging, under the existing rigidity policy. User acceptance pending.

entries.title: Move, dock, select and organize UI
entries.where: UI library; UI edit mode; shared frame/control context actions.
entries.behavior: Drag actual frame handles or supported control edges. Docking offers destinations when a dragged header reaches another header. UI selection, alignment, compaction and reset are separate from knowledge structure. Window/frame drag previews reuse gesture-local target discovery and read-only docking policy results. Visual movement uses the latest pointer position once per animation frame, with geometry reads before transform writes. Release refreshes destination geometry and commits through the existing shared history; cancellation restores the live payload. Active-context shortcuts defer to a held UI gesture, so Esc cancels the drag before a parent minimize action. Pickup snapshots exclude descendants of the held frame/window and read visibility before lifting, reducing the expand-then-drag setup burst.

entries.title: Circular Omnic composer: editing inside, tools on the rim
entries.where: Create → New Omnic object, or select an object → Open Omnic composer. Both open the same circular radar.
entries.behavior: The whole Composer is a circular radar with editing inside and icon tools along its rim. Root tools are hidden by default: hover the shared circular rim axis to reveal them, then move onto a tool. There is no eye/show-hide button. Tools stay revealed while a child category or requested editor is open; keyboard focus on the rim/tools also reveals them. Hover reveal uses CSS without pointer-move matching or recipe/history writes, and registered controls remain mounted. Free/Realistic, ⠒ Atomnic, name/save, File and reset are adjacent rim tools, with pen/eraser last so toggling Atomnic does not shift preceding tools. Presets opens on right-click of empty editing space, not on the rim; it contains existing construction presets, workspace presets and saved operation tools. Categories open smaller child rings at the category click, retaining parent rings/canvas; portals escape frame clipping. Dial centres stay exactly at the invocation point. Atomnic off/on preserves the same recipe and geometry. Direct left-drag moves existing targets; right-click during movement settles it and opens position settings. Wheel over the interior zooms the view (40–1000 extent), preserving browser Ctrl+wheel. Save/copy/import/export, live world drafts, history, recovery and library owners remain shared. Retired Object/Structure/Selection/Transform/Fill-marking/Motion/Inspection wrappers, Configure selected component, Operation scope and View zoom buttons remain absent. Color is a rainbow wheel, Fill ◐ and Opacity a faded ⬤. The last-position pen/eraser button uses the supplied eraser silhouette with upper white/lower black when offering Erase, reversed for Pen. Active cursors now inherit the activated tool icon through the website-wide shared cursor system. The purple hardcoded eraser cursor is removed. Button and cursor share the same two-tone no-underline silhouette; the button offers the next action while the cursor represents the active action. Tool cursor inheritance is now limited to the currently applicable operation zone. Leaving the editing circle for the tool rim or settings restores the normal cursor; returning restores the retained tool. Direct grabs show Move while held, then restore the retained operation. Edited-world image hit tests supply the same boundary rule. Empty-space right-click opens the preset radial. Choosing a preset shows all its currently applicable DOFs together around one circle. Numeric setter spokes appear while pressing/dragging their DOF icons, extending outward with the same length as the owning button diameter. Numeric strips use the shared slider; categorical strips cycle choices, toggles switch on/off, and color strips open the shared color editor. DOF right-click opens shared snap/step configuration. Choosing a preset commits it immediately to the draft. Accepted property changes persist independently; Enter/✓ only finishes editing. Esc/back or empty-space dismissal closes the dial without removing the chosen preset. Contextual dials at every category depth now pack icons around the centre button, using only the space required for the centre, neighbouring icons and any value strips. Fixed oversized dial radii are removed. All popup dials now inherit one radialLayout/RADIAL_GEOMETRY policy: equal centre/button size, count-based nonoverlap and a shared depth progression. Setters do not inflate the button radius. Viewport width no longer squeezes fixed-size slots together; large or edge-opened dials may clip. Automatic More tools overflow is removed everywhere; only explicit categories nest. Appearance DOFs (Color, Opacity and opacity progression) inherit one Appearance category from their shared input metadata in both target and preset dials. The existing mfx effects category lives beneath Appearance. Units/fill controls (Fill, Count, Size, Length, Radius, Stroke width and Stroke progression) inherit the ●● category; position controls (Rotation, Spacing, Gap progression, Centre offset and authored coordinates where applicable) inherit ⟊. Shared input metadata applies the same grouping to preset, target and MC dials. Hovering a category shows its children; leaving the connected category and child dial hides them. Drag a popup dial by its centre circle to reveal the underlying edits. A shared centre slider scales all popup dials from 1× to 2×, including buttons, spacing and spoke setters; the resident canvas size is unchanged. Scale is transient UI presentation and does not edit geometry/history. A category-centre click still goes Back; dragging does not. The origin handle has an interactive button role so shared empty-space dismissal never consumes its drag press. Position is transient and resets on a new invocation/stage. Movement uses only pointer capture and local translation, without scene edits or per-motion geometry queries. Popup buttons pack against their centre without reserving interior space for setters; equisized setter strips extend outward from their owner as radial spokes. Dragging follows the displayed axis, captured only at gesture start. Color has no value strip. Both target and preset DOF sliders are hidden at rest. Press and drag a numeric DOF icon: its spoke slider appears and the same gesture adjusts from the current value without jumping. Release commits and hides the slider; cancellation restores the previous value. Right-click keeps the existing snap/configuration path. Non-numeric tools retain their existing actions. The shared centre size slider remains visible only on the highest popup parent; child dials inherit its scale. Category children open on hover and collapse after leaving the category and its children. Size uses ●⬤ and Radius uses ⊖. The ◎ Nested rings preset inserts a count-controlled ring generator (1–64). Its shared DOFs set innermost radius, radial gap, gap progression, centre drift per ring and direction, fill, stroke width/progression, color, opacity/progression. Defaults are concentric, equally spaced and unfilled. Existing authored ring groups remain editable. Generated ring roles have stable index identities; changing count preserves surviving indices. Generated roles do not yet have individual persistent overrides; use authored rings for independent edits. Invalid extent/work-budget results are rejected. Member and Part / half-unit concept presets are removed from the preset list; existing saved constructions remain intact. All construction and saved presets occupy direct slots around the preset dial; adding presets grows that ring instead of creating an additional-tools submenu. Procedural X/Y inputs no longer appear in preset or target DOF menus or generated Composer parameter editors; position remains available by direct left-drag and its existing movement settings. Left-clicking empty space dismisses all open contextual dials and requested dial editors, consuming that press so it does not also draw or begin a world gesture. Dial ×/close buttons are removed; the middle circle remains an unlabelled origin marker at full opacity. Category Back and Escape still step outward. Controls and rendered target roles retain their own click handling. Empty-space dismissal preserves chosen presets and accepted settings. Line and Ring are standalone presets; Ring no longer inserts an array. Oscillation is removed from construction presets and appears as the sole current motion effect under the rim category labelled/iconed mfx. Effects are discovered from operator metadata. Applying mfx → Oscillation uses selected geometry (the whole composition when no selection exists), adds no new geometry and opens the same radial DOF settings. Reopening the same target effect retains its operation identity/settings. The existing bounded animation preview is started when allowed. Dial centres anchor exactly at their opening click. Entire popup dials default to 100% opacity, including tools and setters; drag the centre circle to see underlying edits. New constructions and workspace presets now insert alongside previous contents at the empty-space click. Internal component/operation/frame identities and scopes are remapped; external object references retain canonical identity. Only the inserted structure becomes selected. MC Active context uses existing Delete, F focus, M edge-fit/restore, W edge-fit/restore, D numeric expansion/compression and Compact commands through a shared target adapter. Multiple compatible DOFs open one shared radial choice before execution; one compatible DOF runs directly. Selected geometry lends existing properties to MC through the common property bindings. Close is not geometry deletion and is unavailable there.

entries.title: Click responsiveness and shared rendering work
entries.where: Ordinary controls, including Omnic library → Objects → Structural filters.
entries.behavior: Render-time function, anchor, owner and icon target lookups share snapshot indexes. Opening/collapsing a frame preserves appearance target metadata when ownership and captions are unchanged. Appearance adjusters reuse target calculations; hidden dock areas skip measurement. Hot function controls now subscribe to their own item, binding, selection and permission slices instead of the full UI context. Stable appearance context actions keep current handlers without broadcasting closure changes. Legacy consumers retain their existing route during incremental migration. Fields, action registrations and embedded headers use scoped subscriptions. Dock workspace geometry/context preserve identity when unchanged; appearance label invalidation follows actual customized owners, not unrelated frame registration order. Floating windows, panels, frame chrome, docking residents and labels now use scoped subscriptions. Closed frame searches and dormant popup adapters do not subscribe to unrelated UI updates. Native caption/button discovery deduplicates inserted subtrees and updates changed hosts directly; unchanged native presentation skips DOM writes and permission work. Discovered function registrations publish once per microtask while commands/history remain synchronous. With no UI controls selected, ordinary layout changes now skip UI-selection discovery and visibility measurement. Subscription snapshot checks reuse pure selector results for the same committed snapshot and selector; changed state or captured props still reevaluate. Window movement now coalesces pointer positions per frame, reuses target lists and caches ownership/pinning/context/docking reads until the layout snapshot changes. Final release refreshes the pointed destination and uses the existing single-commit history path. Newly discovered frame captions now read their initial font sizes together before symbol/tooltip styling writes. This avoids repeated synchronous style recalculation during first-use presentation; later collapse/reopen keeps existing caption state. Drag pickup excludes a frame/window’s own subtree from destination measurements, snapshots visibility before lifting, and uses an exact resident lookup. Final destination refresh and shared docking/history remain intact. Repeated activation of the current front window reuses its existing layer rather than changing z-index and rerendering the wrapper on each grab; other windows still rise. Fixed surfaces already mounted directly on the page move using their existing transform without popover promotion or geometry rewrites. Drag destination bounds are cached on demand; child-slot measurement is limited to destinations actually considered. Cursor-open windows use viewport free placement on both rendering and drop, avoiding workspace packing on release. Drag capture no longer toggles a descendant CSS selector across the whole page. Release deduplicates pointed ancestor measurements, reuses gesture candidate lists. Final placement continues to use the exact release coordinate; no inertia is implemented. Moving an already-free frame validates its new coordinates and preserves unrelated layout records instead of rerunning structural detach/prune/full validation. The held payload now receives a direct transform update from each pointer event; docking discovery/feedback alone stays frame-batched. Movement does not wait for docking calculations or interpolate toward the cursor. Release now hands direct visual ownership back to committed layout synchronously, preventing a paint of the pre-drag position between them. The interface state owner recognizes immutable coordinate-only edits and validates the changed coordinates without rechecking unchanged topology; other edits/imports retain full validation.
